discovery: Quantum cryptography and the foundations of quantum information protocols (BB84, entanglement-based key distribution, quantum teleportation)

nominees.name: Charles H. Bennett
nominees.affiliation: IBM Research, Thomas J. Watson Research Center, USA

nominees.name: Artur Ekert
nominees.affiliation: University of Oxford, UK, and Centre for Quantum Technologies, National University of Singapore

motivation: Bennett and Brassard (BB84, 1984) showed that the quantum laws themselves, not computational assumptions, can guarantee the secrecy of communication. Ekert (1991) linked key security directly to Bell's inequalities, turning a foundational test of nonlocality into a working cryptographic resource. Bennett and Brassard, with colleagues, also proposed quantum teleportation (1993), which experiments have since realized over fibre, free-space and satellite links. Together these insights founded quantum information science as a physical discipline. Information became a physical quantity governed by superposition and entanglement. Their ideas have driven decades of experiments on single photons and entangled states, device-independent security, and intercontinental quantum networks. The field of quantum communication now spans laboratories and industry worldwide. Their work shows how deep questions about the foundations of quantum mechanics can produce entirely new technologies.
